papers.title: Regularization Independence in the One-Dimensional Schrödinger Equation with Delta Potential
papers.abstract: We consider a class of regularizations $\{\delta_\varepsilon\}$ of the Dirac delta defined by a uniform $L^1$ bound, the normalization $\int\delta_\varepsilon\to1$, and a truncated first-moment condition, with no restriction on sign, shape, support, or scaling. For this class we prove that the transmission and reflection coefficients for the Hamiltonian operator $H_\varepsilon=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}-\lambda\delta_\varepsilon$ at fixed energy converge to those of the delta interaction. Under the additional assumption that each $\delta_\varepsilon$ is bounded, we show that any family of negative eigenvalues of $H_\varepsilon$ bounded away from zero converges to $-\lambda^2/4$ when $\lambda>0$, and that no such family exists when $\lambda<0$. Both convergences are obtained with an explicit rate, expressed through two integrals of $\delta_\varepsilon$, directly computable for a given regularization. The bound-state convergence follows from the work of Brasche, Figari, and Teta; here, our contribution is an elementary proof with an explicit rate. Their norm resolvent convergence, however, does not by itself imply convergence of the scattering matrix, which was previously known for families obtained by scaling a single fixed profile; we prove it for a strictly larger class.

papers.title: Strict Monotonicity of the First Positive Steklov Eigenvalue on Eccentric Spherical Shells in Every Dimension
papers.abstract: For $d\ge2$, consider the region between two nested spheres of fixed radii, with the inner sphere translated a distance $\varepsilon$ from the outer center. We prove that the first positive eigenvalue of the Steklov problem, with the spectral boundary condition imposed on both spheres, decreases strictly with $\varepsilon$ throughout the noncontact interval. This settles the planar monotonicity conjecture formulated by Nigam and establishes its higher-dimensional counterparts. In dimension two we use a double-center holomorphic expansion and a pair of positive compact coefficient operators. For every $d\ge3$, solid Gegenbauer harmonics yield analogous axisymmetric and transverse operators, with a positive rank-one monopole correction. Weighted angular-mode comparison for $d\ge3$ and a direct matrix comparison for $d=2$ identify the first positive eigenvalue as the unique level-one crossing of an associated spectral radius. The first eigenspace has dimension $d$ in the concentric case and dimension one for every nonconcentric configuration. Convergence and reconstruction estimates justify the coefficient reductions at the two boundaries.

papers.title: On pseudospectra of the relativistic rotated harmonic oscillator
papers.abstract: We establish an upper bound to the norm of the resolvent of a relativistic version of the non-self-adjoint operator obtained by a dilation analytic transformation of the quantum harmonic oscillator. The estimate implies a decay for large complex energies along rays with angles larger than that of the dilation. In this way we positively answer a question left open in [Proceedings of the Royal Society A 2025].

papers.title: The Pólya--Szegő buckling conjecture in dimensions two through forty-seven
papers.abstract: We prove the P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} buckling conjecture in dimensions $2\le n\le47$: among open sets of prescribed finite volume, a ball minimizes the first clamped buckling eigenvalue. More precisely, we establish the sharp comparison $\Lambda_1\left(\Omega\right)\ge \left(j_{n/2,1}/j_{n/2-1,1}\right)^2 \lambda_1^{\mathrm D}\left(\Omega\right)$, where $\lambda_1^{\mathrm D}$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue and $j_{\nu,1}$ is the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$ of the first kind. The proof extends a radial calibration to all Hessian directions; positive coefficient expansions and logarithmically convex Laplace integrals control the resulting matrix. A Lipschitz construction handles sign changes and arbitrary boundaries. Equality in the volume bound holds precisely for balls modulo sets of zero $H^2$ capacity. We prove that this calibration fails in every dimension $n\ge48$.

papers.title: Counting eigenvalues below the lowest Landau level Robin Dirichlet boundary conditions in an annulus
papers.abstract: We study a charged quantum particle confined to an annulus and subject to a strong uniform magnetic field. A Dirichlet condition is imposed on the inner boundary and a Robin condition on the outer boundary. We are interested in the number of bound states whose energy lies below the lowest Landau level, the threshold set by the magnetic field in the whole plane. In the semiclassical regime, we derive an asymptotic formula for this number. It shows how the count depends on the geometry of the annulus, through the length and curvature of the outer boundary, and on the strength of the Robin parameter. We treat both the repulsive and the attractive cases of the Robin condition and describe how the attractive case changes the boundary behavior that produces these low-lying states. The proof reduces the problem to an effective one-dimensional model near the outer boundary and relies on separation of variables in angular momentum.

papers.title: Counting circles in Kleinian circle packings
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a bounded Kleinian circle packing with symmetry group $\Gamma$, and let $N_{\mathcal{P}}(T)$ denote the number of circles in $\mathcal{P}$ of radius at least $T^{-1}$. We obtain an asymptotic formula for $N_{\mathcal{P}}(T)$ in which the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator below the continuous spectrum contribute a finite sum of main terms, with an error term having the same exponent as in the counting theorem of Lax--Phillips for $\Gamma$-orbits in $\mathbb H^3$.

papers.title: Sharpness of the acceleration-dependent Hölder exponent for the integrated density of states
papers.abstract: We prove that the acceleration-dependent H\"older exponent $1/(2\omega)$ for the integrated density of states is sharp in the supercritical regime. For every positive integer $k$ and every Diophantine frequency, we construct a real even trigonometric polynomial potential of degree $k$ such that, at a spectral edge, the Lyapunov exponent is positive, the acceleration is $k$, and the exact local H\"older exponent is $1/(2k)$. In particular, the $1/2$-H\"older regularity of the subcritical regime for Diophantine frequencies does not hold in general in the supercritical regime. The proof uses Aubry duality and a KAM iteration that adjusts the potential coefficients to make the dual cocycle reducible to a principal unipotent matrix. A comparison with an explicit reference family and symplectic block diagonalization then reduce the IDS estimate to a two-dimensional rotation-number estimate.

papers.title: Quantum unique ergodicity and the critical crossover for 1-d Gaussian band matrices
papers.abstract: We consider an $N\times N$ complex Gaussian random band matrix in one dimension with band width of order $W$, in the periodic block form of Yau and Yin. The $N$ sites are split into $n=N/W$ blocks of size $W$ on a ring, and the entries are nonzero only within a block and between adjacent blocks. The conjectured localization--delocalization transition occurs at $W\sim\sqrt N$. We prove quantum unique ergodicity for bulk eigenvectors at every deterministic rank whenever $W^2/N\to\infty$, with no power or logarithmic separation between $W^2$ and $N$. At the threshold $N/W^2\to\tau\in(0,\infty)$, we show that the rescaled bulk eigenvalues and the block-mass profiles of their eigenvectors (the probability measures on the circle placing at $k/n$ the squared norm of the eigenvector on block $k$) converge jointly to a unique law. This law is encoded by a random entire function whose zeros give the limiting eigenvalues, and its derivatives there give the limiting profile integrals. The law of this function is determined by the Dorokhov--Mello--Pereyra--Kumar (DMPK) diffusion of the unitary class. In the critical law, the profiles have strictly positive variance against every nonconstant smooth test function, so they are not concentrated on the uniform profile. As $\tau\to0$ this variance vanishes and the local spectrum tends to the sine process. As $\tau\to\infty$ it tends to a Poisson process where both limits taken after the critical one. The critical family thus interpolates between the delocalized and localized regimes, confirming for this model the prediction of Fyodorov and Mirlin that at $W^2\asymp N$ the joint law of eigenvalues and eigenvectors depends only on $N/W^2$. The full content of this work has been autoformalized in Lean4 by AxiomProver.

papers.title: Dirac eigenvalue comparison
papers.abstract: We study how curvature bounds control the Dirac eigenvalues of closed spin manifolds, comparing the positive and negative eigenvalues separately. Within a fixed conformal class and spin structure, pointwise ordering of scalar curvature relative to a metric of negative scalar curvature implies comparison at every nonzero index. On the two-sphere, a holomorphic ladder on the half-canonical bundle proves the corresponding comparison in both directions under a Gaussian curvature bound. On surfaces of higher genus, the same bundle identities propagate comparison from the scalar and spinor levels to higher canonical powers. In the round conformal class on the higher dimensional sphere, a prescribed scalar curvature bound yields an upper bound in absolute value for the first $2^{[n/2]}$ Dirac eigenvalues. When the conformal class varies, we can show that the corresponding comparisons on hyperbolic surfaces and odd-dimensional spheres no longer hold; while on even-dimensional spheres, the first gap and all sufficiently high-index eigenvalues of either sign satisfy a one-direction comparison.

papers.title: Generic equivariant simplicity of the spectrum of Laplace-type operators with finite symmetry
papers.abstract: We prove that for generic elements in three natural families of Laplace-type differential operators on smooth manifolds, which are equivariant with respect to a finite symmetry group, all the eigenspaces are irreducible representations. In other words, the spectrum of these operators is generically equivariantly simple. The three families of operators with symmetry are Schr\"odinger operators parametrized by the potential, going back to the work of Wigner, Laplace-Beltrami operators parametrized by invariant Riemannian metrics and conformal Laplacians parametrized by invariant metrics in a given conformal class. The latter two results extend prior work of Zelditch for certain free group actions and resolve, for finite group actions, a well-known open question raised by Guillemin and Yau. Our approach stems from methods developed by Wendl and Doan-Walpuski to address equivariant transversality in symplectic topology.

papers.title: Polarity of the First Dirichlet Liouville Spectral Gap
papers.abstract: We prove zero $1$-capacity of first-gap collisions for the minimal Liouville spectral Green-response form and its canonical extension. The minimal-form diffusion avoids collisions for every initial law absolutely continuous with respect to the spectral law.
